sourceRecords.title: Stillstrom builds 11 kV interface unit for charging vessels in offshore wind farms
sourceRecords.sourceText: Stillstrom reports completion of its 11 kV vessel-mounted charging unit and factory acceptance testing witnessed by DNV. The modular unit can connect offshore wind infrastructure to service-vessel batteries. The wind-farm interface remains in development; extended trials of the complete system are expected in summer 2027.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

sourceRecords.title: Turkish Marine Survey Specialist Wins Work on Country’s First Offshore Wind Site Investigation Programme
sourceRecords.sourceText: offshoreWIND.biz reports that MENR selected DenAr for geophysical and geotechnical investigations at two Sea of Marmara areas under NCS-01. Scope includes sonar, seismic and UXO surveys, seabed cone penetration testing, sampling and laboratory work. This is offshore wind site preparation; neither a floating foundation selection nor a wind-farm construction award is established.
sourceRecords.licenseNote: Public source; concise attributed factual paraphrase and provenance retained, not the full article. No broader republication rights assumed.

briefingItems.title: Stillstrom factory-tests offshore vessel charging unit
briefingItems.oneLineSummary: DNV witnessed factory testing of the vessel-side 11 kV unit; complete-system sea trials remain planned.
briefingItems.explanation: Stillstrom completed its vessel-mounted charging unit and factory tests. The wind-farm interface remains under development, with extended trials of the complete system expected in summer 2027.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The milestone concerns tested vessel-side hardware; full offshore-system trials are still ahead.

briefingItems.title: DenAr selected for Türkiye offshore wind site investigations
briefingItems.oneLineSummary: Reported NCS-01 contract covers geophysical and geotechnical work at two Sea of Marmara areas.
briefingItems.explanation: offshoreWIND.biz reports a DenAr site-investigation contract covering sonar, seismic, UXO and seabed testing. The work prepares offshore wind sites; the report does not establish a floating foundation choice or wind-farm construction award.
briefingItems.whyItMatters: The reported award concerns site data collection ahead of development decisions.

duplicateEventGroups.note: One factory-test milestone with primary and trade provenance.

coverageNotes: Sparse reviewed week: two independent offshore engineering candidates, without padding to five. Search/index access and English-language discovery leave coverage gaps.

Stillstrom primary provenance was found through the approved offshoreWIND.biz discovery source. Its factory-tested vessel unit is not a fully trialled offshore charging system; no floating-specific deployment or cost reduction is claimed.

DenAr remains attributed trade reporting. The company’s matching social post was corroborative only, not an accepted source record; no accessible dated ministry announcement was found. This is offshore site preparation, with no confirmed floating foundation selection.

The Fram award and Frontline trials were covered in the prior edition. New article dates do not make them independent new events; retained as excluded_low_relevance with explicit repeat-event reasons.
Floating OTEC is outside FOWT scope. The German BSH item provides no explicit floating-wind scope. The DeepWind bird article is dated 31 October despite recent search indexing.
